name: IMSMQCMP.jcl
description:
This JCL job (IMSMQCMP) automates the full build pipeline for a CICS/IMS/MQ-integrated COBOL program (IMSMQPGM), performing CICS translation, COBOL compilation, and link-editing to produce a deployable load module. The job takes COBOL source code that integrates CICS transaction processing, IMS database access, and IBM MQ messaging, and produces a ready-to-execute load module stored in the CICS load library.Key Functionalities:
Translates the COBOL source program (IMSMQPGM) using the CICS preprocessor (DFHECP1$) with CICS, DLI (IMS), and COBOL3 options, converting CICS and IMS API calls into standard COBOL statements
Compiles the translated COBOL source using the IBM Enterprise COBOL compiler (IGYCRCTL) with options for non-dynamic linking, object code generation, re-entrant code, and cross-reference/map listings
Prepares the IMS entry point control card (ENTRY IMSMQPGM / NAME IMSMQPGM(R)) for inclusion during the link-edit step
Prepares the CICS language interface stub (DFHELII) link-edit control card to enable CICS runtime communication
Prepares the IBM MQ stub (CSQCSTUB from CSQSTUB) link-edit control card to enable MQ runtime communication
Link-edits all compiled object modules together with the CICS stub (DFHELII), MQ stub (CSQCSTUB), IMS entry point definition, and required system libraries to produce the final executable load module
Stores the final linked load module into the CICS load library (AWS.M2.CICSLOAD) as member IMSMQPGM, making it available for execution under CICS with IMS and MQ connectivity

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The IMSMQPGM source program is submitted for translation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The CICS/IMS Translator reads the source program with CICS, DLI, and COBOL3 modes specified
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program is recognized and processed as a COBOL program that contains both embedded CICS transaction commands and embedded IMS DL/I database access calls

rules.Rule_Name: TRN - DFHECP1$ - Define IMSMQPGM as a Multi-Technology COBOL Program
rules.Rule_Description: IMSMQPGM is defined as a COBOL program that integrates CICS transaction processing commands and IMS DL/I database access calls, requiring specialized translation before it can be compiled.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The build process for IMSMQPGM is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The TRN step is triggered
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Translation executes unconditionally as the first step with no conditions or dependencies on prior steps, ensuring the source is always translated before compilation begins

rules.Rule_Name: TRN - DFHECP1$ - Enforce Translation as Mandatory First Step in Build Process
rules.Rule_Description: Translation of the IMSMQPGM source program is the unconditional first step in the build pipeline — it must always execute before any compilation or packaging steps, with no dependency on prior conditions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The IMSMQPGM source program contains embedded CICS transaction processing commands
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The translator processes the source with the CICS translation mode enabled
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All embedded CICS commands are converted into equivalent standard COBOL statements that can be processed by the COBOL compiler in the subsequent compilation step

rules.Rule_Name: TRN - DFHECP1$ - Translate Embedded CICS Transaction Commands to Standard COBOL
rules.Rule_Description: All CICS transaction processing commands embedded in the IMSMQPGM source must be converted into standard COBOL statements so the program can be processed by the COBOL compiler in the subsequent step.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The IMSMQPGM source program contains embedded IMS DL/I database access calls
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The translator processes the source with the DLI translation mode enabled
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All embedded IMS DL/I calls are converted into equivalent standard COBOL statements that can be processed by the COBOL compiler in the subsequent compilation step

rules.Rule_Name: TRN - DFHECP1$ - Translate Embedded IMS DL/I Database Access Calls to Standard COBOL
rules.Rule_Description: All IMS DL/I database access calls embedded in the IMSMQPGM source must be converted into standard COBOL statements so the program can be processed by the COBOL compiler in the subsequent step.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The translation of IMSMQPGM completes and produces a translated COBOL source
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The translated source file (&&SYSCIN) is created
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The translated source is stored as a temporary file, automatically passed forward to the compilation step for further processing, and permanently discarded after the compilation step consumes it — it is never retained in any permanent application library

rules.Rule_Name: TRN - DFHECP1$ - Manage Translated Source as Temporary Intermediate Artifact
rules.Rule_Description: The translated COBOL source produced by the TRN step is a temporary intermediate artifact that is automatically passed to the compilation step and is never permanently stored in any application library.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The IMSMQPGM source program resides in the application source library (AWS.M2.COBOL.SRC)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The translation step accesses the source program
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The source program is read in shared, read-only mode — the original source remains completely unmodified, and other processes may simultaneously access the same source library during translation

rules.Rule_Name: TRN - DFHECP1$ - Preserve Source Program Integrity During Translation
rules.Rule_Description: The original IMSMQPGM source program must be accessed in shared read-only mode during translation to ensure the source is not modified and remains simultaneously available to other processes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The IMSMQPGM program has completed the prior translation step (TRN)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The return code from any prior step is evaluated before the COBOL compilation step begins
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the return code from any prior step is greater than 4 (indicating a failure), the COBOL compilation step is skipped entirely and no compiled object module is produced; If the return code from all prior steps is 4 or less (indicating success), the COBOL compilation step proceeds and compiles the translated IMSMQPGM source program

rules.Rule_Name: COBOL - IGYCRCTL - Conditional COBOL Compilation Execution
rules.Rule_Description: The COBOL compilation step executes conditionally based on the outcome of the prior translation step (TRN). If translation failed, compilation is bypassed to prevent processing invalid source code.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The IMSMQPGM program is being compiled for deployment in the CICS transaction processing environment
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The COBOL compiler processes any CALL statements found within the IMSMQPGM source program
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All CALL statements must be statically bound and resolved at compile time (NODYNAM), ensuring that all called programs are identified and linked before the program is deployed to CICS — dynamic resolution of calls at runtime is not permitted

rules.Rule_Name: COBOL - IGYCRCTL - Static Program Call Binding for CICS Deployment
rules.Rule_Description: All program-to-program calls within IMSMQPGM must be statically resolved at compile time, which is a mandatory requirement for programs deployed and executed within the CICS transaction processing environment.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The IMSMQPGM program is being compiled for the CICS multi-user transaction processing environment where multiple transactions may invoke the same program simultaneously
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The COBOL compiler compiles the IMSMQPGM source program
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must be compiled with the re-entrant option (RENT), producing an executable that is safe for concurrent use by multiple CICS transactions sharing the same program copy in memory at the same time

rules.Rule_Name: COBOL - IGYCRCTL - Re-entrant Compilation for Concurrent CICS Transaction Support
rules.Rule_Description: The IMSMQPGM program must be compiled as re-entrant to allow multiple concurrent CICS transactions to share the same copy of the program in memory simultaneously without data corruption.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The COBOL compiler encounters a COPY statement while compiling the IMSMQPGM source program
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The compiler searches for the referenced copybook member to resolve the business data structure definition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The copybook libraries must be searched in the following strict priority order — first: Language Environment library (CEE.SCEESAMP); second: CICS copybook library (CICSTS.CICS.SDFHCOB) containing CICS interface data structures; third: IBM MQ copybook library (MQ.SCSQCOBC) containing IBM MQ message queue data structures; fourth and last: Application business copybook library (AWS.M2.COBCOPY) containing application-specific business record layouts and data definitions — the first library in which the copybook member is found is used, and the remaining libraries are not searched for that member

rules.Rule_Name: COBOL - IGYCRCTL - Business Copybook Library Resolution Priority Order
rules.Rule_Description: When the COBOL compiler resolves business data structure definitions (copybooks) referenced in IMSMQPGM, it must search the designated copybook libraries in a strict, predefined priority order to ensure the correct version of each data structure is used.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The translated COBOL source file (&&SYSCIN), produced by the prior TRN translation step, is available as input to the COBOL compilation step
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The COBOL compilation step completes processing of the translated source file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The translated source file (&&SYSCIN) is permanently deleted and is no longer available for any subsequent step or process — it is a single-use intermediate artifact

rules.Rule_Name: COBOL - IGYCRCTL - Translated Source File Disposal After Compilation
rules.Rule_Description: The translated COBOL source file produced by the prior translation step (TRN) is consumed as input to compilation and must be permanently deleted afterward, as it is an intermediate artifact with no further use.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The COBOL compiler has successfully compiled the IMSMQPGM source program
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The compilation step produces the compiled object module
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The compiled object module (&&LOADSET) is retained and passed forward to the link-edit step (LKED), where it will be combined with the CICS runtime interface, IBM MQ messaging interface, and IMS database runtime support to produce the final deployable CICS executable

rules.Rule_Name: COBOL - IGYCRCTL - Compiled Object Module Handoff to Link-Edit Step
rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful compilation, the compiled object module representing the IMSMQPGM business logic must be retained and passed forward to the link-edit step (LKED) for assembly into the final deployable executable.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The COPYIMS step is reached in the build pipeline after the translation step (TRN) and the compilation step (COBOL) have been executed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Any prior step has completed with a return code greater than 4, indicating a failure in translation or compilation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The COPYIMS step is skipped entirely — no IMS entry point or module name instructions are created, and the build pipeline does not proceed with packaging

rules.Rule_Name: COPYIMS - IEBGENER - Conditional Execution of IMS Packaging Step
rules.Rule_Description: The COPYIMS step is governed by a conditional gate that ensures IMS packaging instructions are only prepared when all prior build steps (translation and compilation) have completed without errors. If any prior step failed, this step is bypassed entirely.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All prior build steps (translation and compilation) have completed successfully with a return code of 4 or less, and the COPYIMS step is executing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The IEBGENER utility copies the inline instruction data to the output instruction file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The directive 'ENTRY IMSMQPGM' is written to the link-edit instruction file (&&COPYIMS), designating IMSMQPGM as the single entry point where execution of the business application begins when it is invoked by CICS

rules.Rule_Name: COPYIMS - IEBGENER - Define Executable Entry Point for IMSMQPGM
rules.Rule_Description: Prepares the link-edit directive that designates IMSMQPGM as the starting point of execution. This ensures that when the CICS transaction processing environment invokes the business application, execution begins at the correct and intended entry point.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All prior build steps (translation and compilation) have completed successfully with a return code of 4 or less, and the COPYIMS step is executing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The IEBGENER utility copies the inline instruction data to the output instruction file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The directive 'NAME IMSMQPGM(R)' is written to the link-edit instruction file (&&COPYIMS), naming the final executable 'IMSMQPGM' and instructing the link-edit step to replace any previously deployed version of IMSMQPGM that already exists in the CICS load library (AWS.M2.CICSLOAD)

rules.Rule_Name: COPYIMS - IEBGENER - Name Load Module and Replace Existing Deployed Version
rules.Rule_Description: Prepares the link-edit directive that assigns the official name to the final executable and enforces a replacement policy — ensuring the newly built version always supersedes any previously deployed version of the program in the CICS load library.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All prior build steps (translation and compilation) have completed successfully with a return code of 4 or less, and both the 'ENTRY IMSMQPGM' and 'NAME IMSMQPGM(R)' directives are defined as inline input data
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The IEBGENER utility executes and copies the inline directives to the output dataset
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A temporary instruction file (&&COPYIMS) is created with fixed-block record format (record length 80 bytes, block size 400 bytes), containing both the entry point directive and the module name/replacement directive, and is passed forward exclusively to the link-edit step (LKED) for use in assembling the final deployable IMSMQPGM executable; the file is automatically discarded after the link-edit step consumes it

rules.Rule_Name: COPYIMS - IEBGENER - Create and Forward Link-Edit Instruction File to Deployment Step
rules.Rule_Description: Packages both the entry point directive and the module name directive into a single temporary instruction file and forwards it to the link-edit step. This instruction file is a required input for the final build and deployment step (LKED) to correctly assemble and deploy the IMSMQPGM executable.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The IMSMQPGM build pipeline is in progress and the COPYLINK step is about to be initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Any prior build step — translation (TRN), compilation (COBOL), or IMS instruction preparation (COPYIMS) — has completed with an error code greater than 4
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The COPYLINK step is skipped entirely, no CICS Language Interface instruction file is created, and the build pipeline proceeds to evaluate the next step under the same condition

rules.Rule_Name: COPYLINK - IEBGENER - Conditional Execution of CICS Interface Instruction Preparation
rules.Rule_Description: This rule governs whether the COPYLINK step is allowed to execute based on the cumulative success of all prior build steps in the IMSMQPGM build pipeline. It acts as a gate to prevent unnecessary processing when earlier steps have already failed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All prior build steps — translation (TRN), compilation (COBOL), and IMS instruction preparation (COPYIMS) — have completed successfully with return codes of 4 or less
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The COPYLINK step executes using the IEBGENER file copy utility
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A CICS Language Interface inclusion instruction — specifically 'INCLUDE SYSLIB(DFHELII)' — is written into a new temporary instruction file named &&COPYLINK, and that file is passed forward to the link-edit step (LKED) so that the CICS Language Interface module (DFHELII) is bound into the final IMSMQPGM executable, enabling the program to issue CICS commands at runtime

rules.Rule_Name: COPYLINK - IEBGENER - CICS Language Interface Instruction File Creation and Forwarding
rules.Rule_Description: This rule defines the creation of the CICS Language Interface (DFHELII) inclusion instruction file. The DFHELII module is mandatory for the IMSMQPGM program to communicate with the CICS transaction processing environment at runtime. The instruction file is created as a temporary file and forwarded to the link-edit step (LKED) for binding into the final executable.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The IMSMQPGM application build pipeline is executing and the COPYMQ step is reached
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Any prior build step in the pipeline (TRN, COBOL, COPYIMS, or COPYLINK) has returned an error code greater than 4
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The IBM MQ CICS Stub interface preparation step (COPYMQ) is automatically skipped entirely, preventing the creation of incomplete or invalid IBM MQ interface instructions for the link-edit step

rules.Rule_Name: COPYMQ - IEBGENER - IBM MQ Interface Preparation Conditional Execution
rules.Rule_Description: Controls whether the IBM MQ CICS Stub interface preparation step executes based on the success of all prior build steps in the IMSMQPGM build pipeline.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All prior build steps (TRN, COBOL, COPYIMS, COPYLINK) have completed successfully with a return code of 4 or less, and the COPYMQ step is authorized to execute
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The COPYMQ step executes using the IEBGENER file copy utility with no additional transformation instructions (SYSIN is DUMMY — straight copy only)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The IBM MQ CICS Stub include directive — specifically the instruction to include the CSQCSTUB module from the CSQSTUB library — is written to a new temporary instruction file (&&COPYMQ) and passed forward to the link-edit step (LKED), so that the IBM MQ messaging interface is bound into the final IMSMQPGM executable, enabling the business application to send and receive messages through IBM MQ queues within the CICS transaction processing environment

rules.Rule_Name: COPYMQ - IEBGENER - IBM MQ CICS Stub Include Directive Generation
rules.Rule_Description: Creates and forwards the IBM MQ CICS Stub include directive to the link-edit step, ensuring the IBM MQ messaging interface module (CSQCSTUB) is bound into the final IMSMQPGM executable.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The build pipeline has executed all prior steps: source translation (TRN), COBOL compilation (COBOL), IMS packaging preparation (COPYIMS), CICS interface preparation (COPYLINK), and IBM MQ interface preparation (COPYMQ)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Any one of the prior steps returns a return code greater than 4, indicating a failure or error condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The link-edit step is skipped entirely — no executable load module is assembled or deployed, and the CICS load library remains unchanged

rules.Rule_Name: LKED - IEWL - Conditional Execution of Link-Edit Step
rules.Rule_Description: The link-edit step that assembles the final deployable executable must only execute when all prior build steps have completed without errors. This ensures a broken or incomplete build is never deployed to the CICS environment.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All prior build steps (TRN, COBOL, COPYIMS, COPYLINK, COPYMQ) have completed successfully with a return code of 4 or less, and all four temporary component files are available for processing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The link-edit step executes to assemble the final IMSMQPGM executable
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The components are assembled in the following strict sequence: (1) the CICS Language Interface module (DFHELII) is included first to establish CICS transaction processing connectivity, (2) the IBM MQ CICS Stub module (CSQCSTUB) is included second to establish IBM MQ message queue connectivity, (3) the compiled COBOL business logic object module is processed third as the core application, and (4) the entry point declaration (ENTRY IMSMQPGM) and module name directive (NAME IMSMQPGM with replace flag) are applied last to finalize the executable identity

rules.Rule_Name: LKED - IEWL - Component Assembly Sequence for Executable Build
rules.Rule_Description: The final IMSMQPGM executable must be assembled by processing its components in a strict, predefined sequence. The order ensures that the CICS and IBM MQ runtime interfaces are bound before the business logic, and that the entry point and module identity are applied last.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The link-edit step is assembling the IMSMQPGM executable and encounters external runtime module references that must be resolved from system libraries
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The linkage editor searches for any external module reference not already included via the SYSLIN input stream
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system libraries are searched in the following strict priority order — stopping at the first library where the module is found: (1) IBM MQ runtime library (MQ.SCSQLOAD) is searched first, (2) z/OS core system library (SYS1.LINKLIB) is searched second, (3) Language Environment runtime library (CEE.SCEELKED) is searched third, (4) CICS system load library (CICSTS.CICS.SDFHLOAD) is searched fourth, and (5) IMS system resident library (IMS.SDFSRESL) is searched last

rules.Rule_Name: LKED - IEWL - External Runtime Reference Resolution Priority
rules.Rule_Description: When assembling the IMSMQPGM executable, all external runtime module references must be resolved by searching a defined set of system libraries in a strict priority order. This ensures that the correct version of each runtime module is selected when the same module name may exist in multiple libraries.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The link-edit step is processing the IBM MQ include directive (INCLUDE CSQSTUB(CSQCSTUB)) from the COPYMQ temporary input file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The linkage editor needs to locate and bind the CSQCSTUB module into the IMSMQPGM executable
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The IBM MQ stub library (MQ.SCSQLOAD) is explicitly referenced as the named source library CSQSTUB, ensuring the correct IBM MQ CICS messaging interface module (CSQCSTUB) is located from this dedicated library and permanently bound into the IMSMQPGM executable — enabling IBM MQ message queue operations at runtime within the CICS environment

rules.Rule_Name: LKED - IEWL - IBM MQ Messaging Interface Explicit Binding
rules.Rule_Description: The IBM MQ CICS Stub module (CSQCSTUB) must be explicitly sourced from a dedicated IBM MQ stub library during the link-edit step. This ensures the correct IBM MQ messaging interface is bound into the IMSMQPGM executable, enabling the business application to send and receive messages through IBM MQ queues while operating within the CICS environment.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The link-edit step has successfully assembled all components — CICS Language Interface, IBM MQ CICS Stub, compiled COBOL business logic, and entry point/module name directives — into a complete executable
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The link-edit step completes the assembly of the IMSMQPGM executable
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The final executable load module named IMSMQPGM is written to the CICS load library (AWS.M2.CICSLOAD) as member IMSMQPGM, any previously deployed version of IMSMQPGM in that library is replaced, the CICS load library remains accessible to other users and jobs during this write operation (shared access), and the newly deployed IMSMQPGM program is immediately available for invocation as a CICS transaction

rules.Rule_Name: LKED - IEWL - Business Application Deployment to CICS Load Library
rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful assembly of all components, the final IMSMQPGM executable must be written directly to the CICS load library, replacing any previously deployed version. This makes the latest version of the business application immediately available for CICS transaction execution without any additional deployment steps.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The link-edit step has been provided four temporary input files: the CICS interface directive file (&&COPYLINK), the IBM MQ interface directive file (&&COPYMQ), the compiled business logic object module (&&LOADSET), and the IMS entry point directive file (&&COPYIMS)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The link-edit step reads and processes each temporary input file from the SYSLIN input stream
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Each temporary file is permanently deleted immediately after it is consumed — the CICS interface directive file (&&COPYLINK) is deleted, the IBM MQ interface directive file (&&COPYMQ) is deleted, the compiled business logic object module (&&LOADSET) is deleted, and the IMS entry point directive file (&&COPYIMS) is deleted — none of these intermediate build artifacts are retained after the final executable has been successfully assembled

rules.Rule_Name: LKED - IEWL - Temporary Build Artifact Cleanup
rules.Rule_Description: All temporary intermediate files created during the build pipeline must be permanently deleted once the link-edit step has consumed them. This ensures that stale or partial build artifacts from a previous run do not interfere with future builds.
